newsitem.title: UK: Allders to go ahead with share consolidation.
newsitem.headline: Allders to go ahead with share consolidation.

text.p: UK department store and retail outlet Allders Plc said on Wednesday that it was recommending a consolidation of its share capital on the basis of 15 new shares for every 19 held.
Allders dropped plans for a share consolidation in September 1996 after the government announced amendments to laws governing the availability of tax credits on company distribution.

Following this, the company paid a special dividend of 46p per share in October 1996. It said at the time it intended to put alternative arrangements in place to restore the position of optionholders for the loss of value arising from the special dividend.
Allders took an exceptional charge of 1.5 million stg in its 1996 accounts in case it became necessary to compensate the optionsholders in cash.

"However, the Inland Revenue has advised that a share capital consolidation undertaken now, along the lines originally envisaged, would not result in the provisions of the Finance Act 1997 being applied to the special dividend paid in October," said the firm.
If the share capital consolidation goes ahead the provision will be released this year.
